revision_reason: Adds CONTRACTS.md section 2b's `family` join key to every declared product, which is what makes this group collectable rather than merely valid. Section 2b was settled on main while this component was being taught the route field, and it keys every route on one column called `family` - the parent ASIN on an amazon route, a declared family label on a brand route - so the collector reads `family` off the group file and a declaration carrying only a fingerprint under a different name could not be collected against however well it validated. Each label names the representative actually declared rather than the wider family, because the membership of these families was not established: comparing the twelve declared products against each other proves they are twelve different families, it does not prove what else is in any one of them. So `family_product_ids` holds the single declared id and the family is recorded as UNVERIFIED, with `family_check` saying what was and was not established - section 2b requires a family with no compared sibling to be reported unverified, never verified, and establishing membership needs a catalogue sweep this component does not do. The id-set fingerprint stays in the verification record as the evidence that two labels are not secretly one family. Nothing measured changed: same two members, same twelve product ids, same oldest-end fingerprints, same reach and text fractions, same concentration figures and substitutability reasons, and readings_at_declare is still 0, so this is still declared before any review has been collected.
substitutability_test: Would a consumer shopping for this seed's product consider this company's product instead of it, as a direct alternative for the same need, at the same point of purchase? If yes, it is a peer. Size, country, listing venue and currency are irrelevant to the answer.
